correctness.rationale: Comparing deletion starts i<j gives equality exactly when X_t=X_{t+b} on i≤t<j, so each class of equal outputs is a contiguous run and D_b−1 counts lag-b disagreements. For uniform letters, equalities on a forest are independent Bernoulli(1/q) by revealing tree vertices from roots. Edges at distinct positive lags cannot coincide, so all covariance terms vanish; in order three only triangle terms survive. Writing t=1/q, the joint probabilities for a single, two, and all three triangle agreements are t,t²,t² respectively; the centered disagreement product has expectation −(t²−t³). The triangle exists exactly when a+b=c and the two different middle positions give 2(n−c) triangles. At n=3 there are no admissible triples. An independent literal enumeration of deletion outputs at q=4,n=5 gave −3/16 for (1,2,3), −3/32 for (1,3,4), and zero for (1,2,4) and (2,3,4). The marginal fixed-lag graph consists of b disjoint paths.
residual_risks: This review establishes only the stated uniform, distinct-lag theorem and its stated marginals; no extension to nonuniform sources or repeated lags is inferred.

evidence: For a graph (V,E), the coefficient of the product of the variables of F⊆E in the Potts sum is q^{k(V,F)}. After normalizing by q^{|V|}, this gives all agreement-indicator moments, with no restriction on the graph.
The later joint deletion-ball second-moment record treats arbitrary-position binary deletions. The later read-deletion forest record is a catalogue lead, not inspected full text.

evidence: To get centered disagreements H_e=1/q−J_e, multiply each Potts factor by 1+t_l/q and set v_e=−t_l/(1+t_l/q) for an edge of lag l. After division by q^{|V|}, the coefficient of t_a t_b t_c is the frozen mixed moment, and the coefficient of t_a t_b is the covariance.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Every distinct two-edge set is a forest, so centering cancels its coefficient. For three edges, q^{k(V,F)−|V|} gives zero after centering except on triangles, where it gives −(q−1)/q³; for lags a<b<c the triangle is determined by one left endpoint and the ordering of a,b, possible iff a+b=c. This explicit substitution and low-degree extraction give the entire claimed increment, including sign and count.

evidence: Schoeny et al. express the deletion diversity using run counts in lag-spaced rows (their stated setting is binary and b divides n). The row-run identity translates to disagreements; direct output comparison removes those restrictions.
The partition function uses factors 1+v_e J_e for equal-letter indicators J_e, with a separate variable for each edge.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The distinct-length cumulant is a mixed coefficient of the product of centered edge-indicator factors, on the graph with edges at the three prescribed lags.

Extracting those coefficients reduces immediately to two-edge forests and the two placements of a middle vertex in a triangle. This is demonstrable stronger prior coverage, not a verdict based on a matching title or unavailable text.

value.rationale: The joint statistic is natural and the additive resonance is a useful illustration. The asserted scientific increment nevertheless consists of the constant-degree extraction of the already known exact graph moment identity, on a lag graph whose only three-edge cycles have gaps a,b,a+b. No surviving invariant beyond this direct consequence is established, and there is no substantive repair in merely reframing that calculation.
residual_risks: This judgment is on the particular second/third moment claim, not on the possible value of harder joint distribution or asymptotic questions.
